reels.series: Things Employees Are Afraid to Say
reels.outcome: By the end of this post, viewers will feel their panic at a vague 'got a minute?' is normal and be able to ask one calm question that turns it into a plan.

loops.open: "Got a minute?" Why does your heart race?
loops.payoff: Vague messages can feel like danger, so ask what it's about.
A topic turns panic into a plan: jot 2 notes, then go.

messages.text: Need to talk to you about something.

props.text: Sure! What's it about, so I can bring the right info?

reels.outcome: By the end of this post, viewers will be able to make their wins visible with one short weekly email so mistakes aren't the only thing their boss sees.

loops.open: Your boss only sees your mistakes. Why?
loops.payoff: Wins go quiet, mistakes get noticed.
Make wins visible every Friday, in writing, and keep a copy.

carousels.outcome: By the end of this post, viewers will be able to tell a forgotten promise from a pattern and lock the next promise in with one friendly recap email.

loops.open: Your boss 'forgot' what they promised. Again. Accident or pattern?
loops.payoff: The raise, the day off, the training: all forgotten.
Once is human. Three times is a pattern.

loops.open: So how do you stop it?
loops.payoff: Not by reminding them out loud again.
Recap it in writing the same day.

slides.text: Your boss "forgot" what they promised. *Again.* Accident or pattern?
slides.sub: How to tell, and what to say.

slides.text: The raise. The day off. The training. *All "forgotten."* Does it matter which?
Once is human. *Three times is a pattern.* So how do you stop it?
Reminding them out loud, again. *Spoken promises are easy to forget.* What works?
Recap it in writing, same day. *Emails are hard to forget.* What do you write?
"Thanks for today! Confirming: training approved for March. Let me know if I missed anything."
Follow *@unspokenatwork1* now, or you might never see this page again.
slides.sub: Save this for the next "I forgot."
